Well, that's how you'd d it for Ubuntu and other Debian-based distros...

For Arch (and pacman based distros) it's sudo pacman -Rns $(pacman -Qqtd).

And, to clean the cache, it's sudo pacman -Sc. But I'd be careful with that one... Your cache is there to keep "older" versions of all of your packages so that you can downgrade in the event a program starts crashing, or otherwise messing up your system. Once you clean the cache, all of those "older versions" are removed from your system, and you're stuck with what you have at that point.
